summary: 44-year-old man with a symptomatic reducible umbilical hernia, 2 cm defect on examination. EHS/AHS 2020: mesh repair (open preperitoneal flat mesh suggested) for defects ≥1 cm.

inputs.hpi: One year of a bulge at the belly button that is sore after football. Pushes back easily. No vomiting, bowels normal.

exam.abdomen: Soft, non-tender. Reducible umbilical hernia, fascial defect about 2 cm, cough impulse, skin normal. No divarication. No other defects.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Umbilical hernia, reducible, 2 cm defect
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Reducible umbilical hernia, 2 cm defect, symptomatic. Elective open mesh repair (preperitoneal flat mesh). Smoking cessation advised before surgery.

mustRankTopK.knownGapNote: PANE top 3 = inguinal hernia (male x5), cholecystitis, GORD; umbilical_hernia (0.03, umbilical_swelling 0.90) is outranked. PANE: unlisted features count at DEFAULT_SENSITIVITY 0.30 for every disease and there is no false-positive term, so high-prior abdominal diseases (cholecystitis 0.15, GORD 0.12, PUD 0.10; male inguinal hernia x5) outrank the organ-specific disease after a single non-abdominal feature.
mustRankTopK.proposedFix: Model P(feature | not disease) or use a low default sensitivity (e.g. <=0.05) for features outside a disease's system; restrict the candidate set by the presenting system (breast / neck / groin).

mustInclude.note: EHS/AHS 2020: mesh repair suggested for defects ≥1 cm (preperitoneal flat mesh, open).

mustInclude.knownGapNote: The umbilical_hernia protocol has no pre-operative optimisation (smoking) step.

mustExclude.note: An inguinal TAPP operative plan is the wrong template for an umbilical hernia.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: computeClinicalPrompts fires the hernia pathway for any CC/exam containing "hernia", "inguinal" or "umbilical", and always attaches the adult "LAPAROSCOPIC INGUINAL HERNIA REPAIR (TAPP)" operative plan. Here also "EMERGENCY" because "non-tender" matches "tender".
mustExclude.proposedFix: Choose the operative template by hernia site (umbilical/ventral vs inguinal) and make the tender check negation-aware.

guideline.name: EHS/AHS guidelines — treatment of umbilical and epigastric hernias
guideline.section: Indication for repair; mesh vs suture by defect size; open preperitoneal flat mesh; patients with liver cirrhosis and ascites
guideline.citation: Henriksen NA, Montgomery A, Kaufmann R, et al. Guidelines for treatment of umbilical and epigastric hernias from the European Hernia Society and Americas Hernia Society. Br J Surg. 2020;107:171–190.

rationale: Base umbilical case. Checks recognition and the EHS/AHS mesh recommendation, and that templates for another hernia type are not proposed.
